name: Berlyne's Arousal Theory of Aesthetics
citation: Berlyne, D.E. (1971). Aesthetics and psychobiology. Appleton-Century-Crofts.

constructs.description: Properties of stimuli that evoke arousal: novelty, complexity, surprisingness, incongruity, and ambiguity. Together they index prediction error magnitude and perceptual organization cost.
Optimal arousal (Goldilocks principle): intermediate complexity/novelty produces maximum aesthetic pleasure. Extreme values (boredom, confusion) reduce preference.
High arousal triggers exploratory behavior and cognitive engagement. Organism seeks to resolve incongruity and restore predictability, which when successful yields positive affect.

provenance.historical_context: Berlyne formalized the relationship between collative variables (novelty, complexity, incongruity) and hedonic value. The inverted-U prediction became the dominant model for aesthetic preference until processing fluency challenged it in the 2000s.
